clue.text: Look! Some cheap pearls!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A street hawker cries out to passers-by about a tray of cut-price pearls.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to look or seem, as in 'he looks tired'.

clue.text: Roguish but formal when put in the pig pen

indicators.note: the clue says the answer, placed inside the pig pen, makes the word for formal, so removing the pen leaves it

parts.note: starchy means stiffly formal
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: Someone mischievous turns prim once shut up in a pigsty.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtractive clue: 'when put in the pig pen' says the answer sits inside the pen to make the word for formal, so removing the pen recovers it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch describes a knowing, mischievous manner, a synonym of roguish.

clue.text: Investment scheme keeps a small sum of money in liquid food

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the scheme's letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: a PEP was a Personal Equity Plan, a British tax-free investment scheme
a sou was a French coin of tiny value, hence a trifling sum

explanation.surface: A savings plan has a little money tied up in a liquid asset.
explanation.walkthrough: A PEP was a UK tax-free savings scheme of the 1980s and 90s.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea soup is a thick soup, a food eaten as a liquid.

clue.text: Go below broken stair to show style

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means this piece comes after the other
a broken stair is smashed up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a go is a try, an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone is told to step down past a damaged stair to demonstrate their grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' signals the anagram of the stair; 'below' places the attempt after it, which works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill and flair, which is what style shows.

clue.text: She was patient, awfully glad when about to get up

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the other piece
awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: A long-suffering woman was terribly pleased when finally ready to get out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles the letters of the glad (giving GLDA), and 'about' wraps them round the word for getting up. 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Griselda is the proverbially patient wife of medieval tales by Boccaccio and Chaucer.

clue.text: Pious Paul ain't amazingly large

parts.note: Paul Revere was the American patriot famed for his midnight ride

indicators.note: amazingly implies something astonishing has happened to the letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A devout man named Paul, it seems, is remarkably big.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverential means showing deep respect or reverence, close to pious.

clue.text: The queen in an old corset wanders off

indicators.note: in places the queen inside the corset

parts.note: stays is the old word for a laced corset
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A monarch squeezed into an antique corset slips away.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander away from where one should be.

clue.text: Help ruffian to come round if knocked down

indicators.note: come round means encircle, so the ruffian goes around the help

parts.note: a lout is a rough, uncouth man
aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a thug to come over and revive them after being floored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come round' reads like recovering consciousness, apt for someone knocked down, but here it means one word encircling the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid out means flattened, as by a punch that knocks someone to the floor.

clue.text: Financial backer meets an old fool for tea

parts.note: an angel is an investor who backs a venture, especially a theatre show
cake is a dated word for a foolish person

explanation.surface: A theatre investor meets a silly old person for afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: angel cake is a light sponge served at tea time.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel cake is a light sponge cake, a classic item served at afternoon tea.

clue.text: Semi-cryptic keeps a newspaper subtle

indicators.note: keeps means holds, so the half word goes around the rest
semi means half, so only the first half of the word is used

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A half-cryptic puzzle in a paper turns out quite clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Semi' takes the first half of 'cryptic', and 'keeps' says that half wraps round the A and the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafty means cunning and artful, a sense of subtle as in a subtle plot.

clue.text: Declaring a little way to keep doing wrong

parts.note: Av is a short form of avenue, a way
erring is going wrong, doing wrong repeatedly

explanation.surface: Someone swears that a short street has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: AV is the abbreviation of avenue; 'little' signals the shortening. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly, so averring is declaring.

clue.text: Unwanted singleton holds nitwit to be sweet

parts.note: a gooseberry is the unwanted third person with a couple
a fool is a nitwit

explanation.surface: A lonely third wheel puts up with an idiot to stay pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: To play gooseberry is British for being the unwelcome extra with a couple. 'holds' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gooseberry fool is a British dessert of fruit puréed with cream, a pudding or sweet.

clue.text: Lives in a bookshop!

parts.note: lives reads as a verb about someone dwelling among books, but means written accounts of people's lives on the shelves

explanation.definitionFit: Life stories written about people are shelved in bookshops under this heading.

clue.text: Delivery of the Guardian, perhaps, with circular

parts.note: the Guardian is an example of a newspaper
round means circular

explanation.surface: A newspaper delivery comes with a leaflet stuffed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the Guardian as an example. 'circular' looks like a junk-mail leaflet but means ROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper round is a regular route delivering newspapers to homes.

clue.text: The leader unfolds map with a creek to be seen

indicators.note: unfolding a map opens it out, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A guide opens a map to locate a creek.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacemaker leads a race and sets the speed for the others.

clue.text: Italian mother in old radio comedy

parts.note: It is an abbreviation for Italian, as in It vermouth
ma is mother

explanation.surface: An Italian mama appears in a vintage wireless show.
explanation.walkthrough: ITMA (It's That Man Again) was a wartime BBC radio comedy show.
explanation.definitionFit: ITMA was a celebrated BBC radio comedy series of the 1940s.

clue.text: Say nice things about fat rising

parts.note: butter is a fat
up means rising

explanation.surface: Compliment the fat that is going up in price.
explanation.definitionFit: To butter someone up is to flatter them to win favour.

clue.text: They transport 100 seamen

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
ABs are able seamen

explanation.surface: Vehicles carry a hundred sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabs are taxis, which carry passengers about.

clue.text: Good French motorists touring New Zealand finding sudden wealth

parts.note: bon is French for good

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the motorists surround the country

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: French drivers on a tour of New Zealand strike it rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association. 'finding' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonanza is a windfall or sudden source of great riches, originally a rich ore vein.

clue.text: Well-spoken "dirty rat" with one copper behind

indicators.note: dirty suggests the word is soiled and messed up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
late means behind time

explanation.surface: A clearly spoken villain calls someone a dirty rat, with a policeman on his tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dirty' rearranges RAT to ART. 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Articulate means able to speak fluently and clearly.

clue.text: Mean girl gets squeezed in time

indicators.note: squeezed in means placed inside, so the girl goes within the time

parts.note: an age is a period of time
Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An unkind girl is pressed for time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective about the girl, but it is the arithmetic mean.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the mean is the average of a set of values.

clue.text: Floater, one joining church to criticise

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
CE is the Church of England
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Someone drifting joins a church only to find fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floater' could be a person or a voter; here it is something floating on water.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice pan is a slab of floating ice, a drifting floe.

clue.text: Governing bodies holding Sicilian item up

annotationWithheld.why: Governing bodies holding Sicilian item up (14): MUNICIPALITIES is SICILIAN ITEM rearranged around UP, but the clue has no anagram signal unless 'up' does that job while also giving UP
annotationWithheld.clue: Governing bodies holding Sicilian item up

clue.text: It's a strain to work in an office

definitions.meaning: a kind or variety, as a strain of a plant is
to key in text on a keyboard, as office staff do

explanation.surface: Office work is described as a strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Type means a kind or strain, and as a verb means to key text, an office task.

clue.text: No big deal at Lord's in star match

parts.note: a king is a star, the top figure in a field
a pair is a match, two things that go together

explanation.surface: A cricket disappointment comes in a celebrity fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground. A king pair is a batter out first ball in both innings, a duck twice, so 'no big deal' means no runs at all.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a king pair is getting out first ball in both innings, scoring nothing.

clue.text: Ingratiating when interrupting 19th century PM

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Earl Grey was British Prime Minister in the 1830s
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A Victorian-era statesman is cut short by a fawning remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasy can mean unctuous and oily in manner, trying to win favour.

clue.text: McCoy's quality, having a cape of authority

parts.note: real is an old word for royal, as in real tennis, the game of kings
a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Orford Ness

explanation.surface: A man named McCoy is distinguished by a cloak of command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the real McCoy' means the genuine article. REAL in the sense of royal survives in 'real tennis'. 'having a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The real McCoy is the genuine thing, so his defining quality is genuineness.

clue.text: Each expert pilot must swallow some pastry

indicators.note: swallow means take inside, so the pilot goes around the pastry

parts.note: an ace is a top fighter pilot
a pie is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: A star flyer has to wolf down a pastry apiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means for each one, as in 'a pound apiece'.
